newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian airline switches Kinshasa flights to Congo.
newsitem.headline: Belgian airline switches Kinshasa flights to Congo.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena has cancelled all stops at the Zairean capital Kinshasa and is diverting its flights to Congo's capital Brazzaville, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Friday.

Zairean rebels, led by Laurent Kabila, have won control of around three-quarters of the central African nation and are now approaching Kinshasa, which they have threatened to attack if ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko does not resign.

"The ministries of foreign affairs and communications, in consultation with Sabena, have decided to follow the decision made by Air France and SwissAir -- that is, no longer to land at Kinshasa but at Brazzaville," Dehaene told Belgian radio in an interview broadcast on Friday.

"I think it's an elementary security measure seeing as the rebels are not far from (Kinshasa's) airport and we mustn't take pointless risks," he added, while saying there did not seem to be any immediate danger.
Dehaene was speaking from Romania where he is on an official visit.

Belgium this week sent a further 54 paratroopers to Brazzaville to assist in any evacuation of its nationals from Kinshasa, raising to more than 700 the number of Belgian troops now ready to take part in "Operation Greenstream".
"We're in permanent contact with the American and French (forces there)...so that any action would be concerted," Dehaene added.
Meanwhile diplomatic efforts continue to try to find a negotiated solution to Zaire's civil war, and for Mobutu and Kabila to work out a transitional government to put Zaire on a path to democracy.
"I still hope...that the pressure put on Mr Kabila by the United States and South Africa will enable the transition to be carried out without it leading to fighting," Dehaene said.
Belgium, Zaire's former colonial ruler, has recommended its nationals leave the country. But several hundred, including many missionaries, are believed to have stayed.
